title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this page belongs to the 'variations sur l'équation des lacets' manuscript, Grothendieck's continuation of La Longue Marche. In it he studies solutions of the 'loop equation' attached to a pair of generators (rho of order 3, sigma of order 2) of a PSL2(Z)-like group, inside a (profinite) group M.

Objects. Z^!_{rho,sigma} = M^![0] is a group of 'admissible' elements u. To each u he attaches:
- signs eps_2(u), eps_3(u) in {±1}. These are characters; eps_3(u) = 1 iff the corresponding a fixes rho (a(rho) = rho).
- a normalised element a = eps_3(tau') alpha^{-1} u in N'_rho, with a ≡ eps_3(sigma)^{-1} u mod hat-Pi_0.
- b = beta^{-1} u.
This gives a set-theoretic bijection A: u ↦ (u, a, b) onto the solution set S_0 Gamma^!_{rho,sigma}.

Question. Is A multiplicative, i.e. does u'' = u'u give a'' = a'a? The previous page shows a'' ≡ eps · eps_3(sigma)(a') · a mod hat-Pi_0, where eps = -1 iff eps_3 = eps'_3 = -1. Hence a'' = a'a (equivalently a'' ≡ a'a mod hat-Pi_0) iff condition (54): eps_3(sigma)(a') ≡ eps a'.

Case analysis on this page:
- (55a) If eps_3 = 1, (54) is trivial.
- (55b) If eps_3 = -1, (54) reads sigma a' sigma^{-1} ≡ eps'_3 a'. In the quotient M/hat-Pi_0 the classes of sigma and of these elements commute up to a central sign, so this is the commutator identity [sigma., a'.] = eps'_3.
- (56) Since a' ≡ u' or sigma^{-1}u', and sigma commutes with itself, this is equivalent to [sigma., u'.] = eps'_3.
- (57) From the earlier relation (35), u'(sigma) = eps_2(u') sigma, so [sigma., u'.] = eps_2(u').
- (58) Hence the condition becomes eps_2(u') = eps_3(u').

Proposition (completed on the next page). a'' = a'a holds iff eps_3(u) = 1 or eps_2(u') = eps_3(u'). Several equivalent forms are listed: with a' or u', and with sigma acting on a' or a' acting on sigma.

Corollary (next page). A restricted to either of the two index-≤2 subgroups is a multiplicative bijection, but A is not multiplicative on all of Z^!:
- Z^{!!} = {eps_3 = 1};
- Z^{!!!} = {eps_2 = eps_3}.
In effect, on Z^! the map is multiplicative only up to a sign-twist, i.e. a crossed-homomorphism-type correction governed by the characters eps_2 and eps_3. The purpose is to identify the group structure on the set of solutions of the loop equation (GT-type objects) via an explicit group of 'u' elements.
errors: The passage from the commutator in a' to the commutator in u' in (56) silently uses that M/hat-Pi_0 is (locally) a central extension by {±1} in which commutators with sigma are bimultiplicative and [sigma,sigma] = 1. This is consistent with (35) but not restated.
eps''_3(tau') = eps'_3(tau') eps_3(tau') needs tau' to be an involution (or tau'^2 trivial modulo the relevant subgroup) when eps_3 = eps'_3 = -1. This is implicit.
In the proposition the subscript is written Z^!_{rho,r}; it should be Z^!_{rho,sigma}, as on the next page.

ideas.what: Criterion for multiplicativity of the parametrisation u ↦ (a,b) of solutions of the loop equation: a''=a'a iff eps_3(u)=1 or eps_2(u')=eps_3(u')
ideas.modern_name: Group structure on solutions of pentagon/hexagon-type (Grothendieck–Teichmüller) equations; sign-twisted (crossed) homomorphism
ideas.usually_credited_to: GT group: Drinfeld (1990), Ihara; this specific computation not in literature

ideas.what: Using the quotient M/hat-Pi_0 where generators commute up to a central sign, so conditions reduce to commutator identities [sigma,u]=±1 expressed via characters eps_2, eps_3
ideas.modern_name: Central extension by Z/2 / commutator pairing in a class-2 quotient

ideas.what: Two index-2 subgroups {eps_3=1} and {eps_2=eps_3} on which the set bijection becomes a group isomorphism
ideas.modern_name: Index-2 subgroups cut out by sign characters (cf. sign characters on GT-type/Teichmüller groups)

deep.surprise_reason: Careful but routine bookkeeping of signs in a central-extension quotient, establishing when a parametrisation is multiplicative. Interesting as a window into Grothendieck's unpublished GT-type computations, but contains no idea a specialist would find new or surprising.
transcription_corrections: Circled number at top is Grothendieck's pagination (598); archive page number 588 is at bottom left.
In (56) the right-hand side is ε'_3 u' (with ε'_3, not ε_3), as the image shows ε'_3 over the struck E.
Margin note 'NB ε_3=ε_3(u)=ε_3(a), ε'_3=ε_3(u')=ε_3(a'), ε''_3=ε_3(u'')=ε_3(a'')' is correctly placed as a marginal addition beside the Proposition.
'(équivalence aussi bien pour ε'_3=1 que ε'_3=-1)': 'vérifiée' struck and replaced by 'équivalence' written above.
